$comment: Classification layer for `scripts/secrets_inventory.py`. Declares, for every GitHub
Actions secret name in the Fuze fleet, WHERE it is supposed to exist and whether the
value is shared fleet-wide or must be unique per repo.
THIS FILE IS THE MAP, NOT THE MECHANISM. The propagation mechanism already exists and
lives in FuzeSDLC: scripts/provision_secrets.py + .github/workflows/provision-secrets.yml
(workflow_dispatch mode=apply, weekly presence audit). Its FLEET_SOURCED frozenset is the
authoritative list of names it can actually hand out, and its SRC_<NAME> env block in the
workflow is the source-of-truth store. A `propagation: fleet` rule here whose name is NOT
in FLEET_SOURCED is a rule nothing can satisfy automatically -- those carry
`fleetSourced: false` below and are the standing work item.
propagation:
fleet       every onboarded repo needs it (a canonical workflow-template references it)
conditional only repos with a given capability/workflow need it
hub-only    belongs to exactly ONE repo; a copy anywhere else widens blast radius
per-repo    every repo that has it holds its OWN value
external    third-party credential owned by the repo that uses it
sharing:
shared-value one value, copied verbatim to every repo that needs it
unique-value each holder must have a distinct value; copying is a security defect
n/a          single holder, sharing is not a question
severity (fleet/conditional only):
required  the workflow fails or the capability is dead without it
degrades  the workflow skips a step or falls back; absence is tolerable but reduces function

rules.name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
rules.notes: Primary model credential for claude.yml / harden-gate / governance-nightly / fuze-code-review. One account key; per-repo keys would only fragment billing.
rules.description: A direct Anthropic API key, bypassing the in-cluster gateway.
usedBy: claude.yml only -- a workflow titled 'Claude (DISABLED -- replaced by fuze.yml)' whose `on:` block is workflow_dispatch only
rules.scenario: The LiteLLM gateway is unreachable (cluster down, NetworkPolicy change, gateway pod crashlooping) and someone needs an agent run anyway. They manually dispatch claude.yml, which talks to Anthropic directly with this key.
rules.withoutIt: The manual break-glass path is unavailable. No automatic workflow is affected in FuzeInfra today.
rules.whyThisSharing: One Anthropic account key. Per-repo keys would fragment billing without changing blast radius.
rules.note: INTENT vs CODE -- do not document one as the other. The INTENDED design (FuzeSDLC's canonical templates, via the fuze-code-action -> llm-endpoint composite actions) is LiteLLM-first with direct provider keys as fallback. FuzeInfra's DEPLOYED workflows do not implement it: both composite actions exist under .github/actions/ and are invoked by ZERO workflows. Today this key is a MANUAL break-glass, not an automatic fallback. The owner has confirmed the non-adoption is an unfinished migration, not a deliberate opt-out.

rules.name: FUZESDLC_DEPLOY_KEY
rules.notes: Read-only deploy key that lets governance-sync.yml fetch the private FuzeSDLC canonical. Read-only + single-purpose is exactly what makes one shared key acceptable here.
rules.description: A READ-ONLY SSH deploy key for the private izzywdev/FuzeSDLC repository. It authorises `git clone` of the governance hub and nothing else -- no push, no API scope, no access to any other repo.
rules.scenario: You open a PR on FuzeMarket. governance-sync.yml checks out the PR head, uses this key to SSH-clone FuzeSDLC at the repo's declared `baselineRef`, and runs scripts/governance_sync.py to diff the repo's managed files (.claude/agents/**, agent-templates/**, .github/actions/**, .claude/skills/**) against the canonical. Drift is overwritten with the canonical version and committed back to the PR branch before CI runs.
rules.withoutIt: The workflow hits an explicit guard (`elif [ -z "$KEY" ]`) and skips with a ::notice::. The run is GREEN. Nothing is compared, so the repo silently diverges from the fleet baseline -- stale agents, missing skills, framework gaps -- and the divergence is invisible until someone re-runs sdlc-bootstrap.sh by hand.
rules.whyThisSharing: One key, read-only, pointed at ONE shared source repo. Read-only plus single-purpose is what makes a shared value acceptable: a leaked copy grants read of a repo every holder already reconciles against, and nothing anywhere else. Contrast DESIGN_APPROVAL_DEPLOY_KEY, which WRITES to its own repo and therefore cannot be shared.

rules.name: FUZE_AGENT_APP_ID
rules.notes: The org-wide fuze-agent GitHub App (App ID 4729776). Not secret in any real sense -- an App ID is public metadata -- but stored as a secret so the workflow templates can reference it uniformly.
rules.description: The App ID of the org-wide `fuze-agent` GitHub App (App ID 4729776). Not secret in any meaningful sense -- an App ID is public metadata -- but stored as a secret so the templates can reference it uniformly alongside the private key.
usedBy: canonical templates claude-auto-pr.yml, governance-sync.yml, a2a-maintain.yml, mcp-maintain.yml
rules.scenario: An agent workflow needs to open a PR. It exchanges this App ID plus the private key for a short-lived installation token via actions/create-github-app-token, and opens the PR as the App installation identity -- so the PR gets CI runs like a human's would.
rules.withoutIt: The workflow falls back to a bot PAT, then GITHUB_TOKEN. A PR opened by GITHUB_TOKEN is frozen as `action_required` on public repos and gets no runs at all on private ones -- see docs/agent-pr-ci-reachability.md.
rules.whyThisSharing: One App serves the whole org, so there is exactly one ID and one key. Sharing is not a choice.
rules.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-31: present in 22/22 repos and referenced by ZERO DEPLOYED workflows -- the single hit was a canonical template, not a stamped copy. The identity fix is fully staged and completely unwired. Root cause is distribution: governance-sync is detect-only for .github/workflows/**.

rules.name: FUZE_AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
rules.notes: PEM for the same App. Necessarily shared -- one App, one key. Blast radius is the whole fleet, so rotation is a fleet-wide event; the App path is preferred over per-repo PATs precisely because there is ONE thing to rotate.
rules.description: The PEM private key of the org-wide `fuze-agent` GitHub App. Exchanged with the App ID for a short-lived installation token so agent-opened PRs carry a real installation identity and therefore receive CI runs.
usedBy: canonical templates claude-auto-pr.yml, governance-sync.yml, a2a-maintain.yml, mcp-maintain.yml
rules.scenario: An agent workflow needs to open a PR. It exchanges this App ID plus the private key for a short-lived installation token via actions/create-github-app-token, and opens the PR as the App installation identity -- so the PR gets CI runs like a human's would.
rules.withoutIt: The workflow falls back to a bot PAT, then GITHUB_TOKEN. A PR opened by GITHUB_TOKEN is frozen as `action_required` on public repos and gets no runs at all on private ones -- see docs/agent-pr-ci-reachability.md.
rules.whyThisSharing: One App serves the whole org, so there is exactly one ID and one key. Sharing is not a choice.
rules.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-31: present in 22/22 repos and referenced by ZERO DEPLOYED workflows -- the single hit was a canonical template, not a stamped copy. The identity fix is fully staged and completely unwired. Root cause is distribution: governance-sync is detect-only for .github/workflows/**.

rules.name: FUZESDLC_AGENT_PUSH_TOKEN
rules.notes: publish-expert.yml pushes the repo's expert agent definition back to FuzeSDLC. The workflow is stamped into every onboarded repo, so the token has to be too.
rules.description: A fine-grained GitHub PAT scoped to izzywdev/FuzeSDLC ONLY, with Contents + Pull requests read/write. A propose-only credential: it can push a branch and open a PR on the governance hub, and the hub's own agent-sync-guard.yml constrains what that PR may touch. It grants nothing on any other repo.
rules.scenario: You edit .claude/agents/fuzeinfra-expert.md and merge to main. publish-expert.yml reads the `expert` field from .fuze/manifest.json, clones FuzeSDLC with this token, copies the file to agents/fuzeinfra-expert.md, force-pushes branch agent-sync/fuzeinfra and opens a PR. agent-sync-guard.yml verifies the PR touches only that repo's own expert file, then it merges -- and every OTHER repo picks the update up through governance-sync, which uses the separate read-only FUZESDLC_DEPLOY_KEY.
rules.withoutIt: A silent green notice: `::notice::FUZESDLC_AGENT_PUSH_TOKEN not set -- skipping expert publish.` then `exit 0`. Nothing is published. The hub's copy of that repo's expert freezes permanently, because governance-sync deliberately never reconciles a repo's OWN expert -- the repo is upstream of the hub for that one file, and nothing else updates it.
rules.whyThisSharing: Shared today, and the hub's own governance/agent-ownership.md flags it as a known gap rather than a design: 'With a shared push token, repo A could open a PR on branch agent-sync/b; the damage is bounded to one repo edits another's expert file.' The bound comes from the hub-side path guard, not from the token. Per-repo tokens would be strictly better now that provision_secrets.py can fan out distinct values.
rules.note: Push, not pull, is deliberate: a pull model would require the hub to hold credentials into every repo. The rule is 'no repo holds credentials to another repo, and the hub holds none to the repos'. TO BE RETIRED once the fuze-agent App is wired into publish-expert.yml -- but not before, since it was only propagated to the fleet on 2026-08-31 and retiring it now would re-break the 17 repos that just started publishing.

rules.name: LITELLM_FUZE_KEY
rules.notes: Minted in-cluster by FuzeInfra scripts/mint-litellm-fuze-key.sh, held centrally by FuzeSDLC. Referenced by harden-gate, governance-nightly, nightly-integration, a2a-maintain, mcp-maintain, fuze-code-review -- i.e. the always-installed stack.
rules.description: A SCOPED LiteLLM virtual key ($100/30d budget, 7-model allowlist) for the self-hosted LiteLLM proxy running in-cluster at http://litellm.fuzeinfra.svc.cluster.local:4000. The gateway speaks the Anthropic Messages format, so a workflow uses it by pinning ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to that address and passing this key where an Anthropic key would go.
rules.scenario: The nightly sweep needs a model. It pins ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to the in-cluster gateway and authenticates with this key. The gateway routes to whichever provider is healthy -- routerSettings.fallbacks is claude-* -> gpt-4.1 -> gemini-flash-latest -- and the caller sees a normal 200 without knowing which served it. Spend is attributed to this key's own alias in the cost report.
rules.withoutIt: In FuzeInfra's DEPLOYED workflows there is no automatic fallback: fuze.yml preflights the gateway and hard-fails with a Telegram alert. Agent CI for that repo stops.
rules.whyThisSharing: One gateway, one scoped consumer key. The budget and model allowlist -- not the identity -- are what bound this credential.
rules.note: Minted by scripts/mint-litellm-fuze-key.sh; it is runtime state in LiteLLM's Postgres, so it cannot be declared in values.yaml and Argo will never reconcile it. Distinguish from LITELLM_MASTER_KEY (gateway ADMIN, FuzeInfra only) and LITELLM_CI_KEY (intended for a2a-maintain, never minted -- so that workflow currently falls through to the MASTER key on every PR).

rules.name: GH_RELEASE_PAT
rules.notes: One release-bot identity whose whole purpose is that ITS pushes trigger CI, which the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN deliberately cannot do. The current FuzeSDLC templates reference it from governance-sync.yml and claude-auto-pr.yml too, but the copies actually stamped into the repos do not yet -- so scope it to the repos with a release.yml rather than declaring a fleet gap the running CI does not have. Re-check after the next governance-sync ripple. FuzeBI additionally references a legacy alias, FUZEBOT_TOKEN, which has never been set anywhere; retire that name in favour of this one.
rules.description: A classic PAT belonging to a real collaborator account, with `repo` scope. Its whole purpose is that pushes made with it TRIGGER further workflow runs, which the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN deliberately cannot do.
usedBy: canonical claude-auto-pr.yml + governance-sync.yml (not yet in every stamped copy)
rules.scenario: A PR merges to FuzeCall main. release.yml builds and pushes the images, then bump-prod-values must commit the new SHA into deploy/helm/fuzecall/values-prod.yaml. Pushed with this PAT, the new head triggers CI, checks go green, auto-merge lands it and Argo syncs the new tag to prod.
rules.withoutIt: The same commit pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN lands but carries ZERO check runs -- GitHub's deliberate loop-guard. Branch protection then waits forever for checks that will never appear, the bump PR can never satisfy the ruleset, and prod stays pinned to the OLD image while the release reports green. Observed live on FuzeSocial#81.
rules.whyThisSharing: One release-bot identity. The requirement is that the pusher is a collaborator rather than the Actions app -- not that the identity differs per repo.
rules.note: WRONG TIER, being replaced. `repo` scope grants full read/write on every repo its owner can reach, attributes automated commits to a person, and is one shared value across 12 repos. The fuze-agent App installation token is scoped, ~1h lived and also triggers CI. See .github/actions/fuze-push-identity (FuzeSDLC PR #250). FuzeBI additionally references a legacy alias FUZEBOT_TOKEN set in NO repo; retire that name in favour of this one.

rules.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
rules.notes: One bot serves the whole fleet. telegram-pr-merged.yml is stamped everywhere and calls the FuzeSDLC reusable with `secrets: inherit` -- so a repo without this token has a merge notifier that silently never fires. NOT in FLEET_SOURCED: add SRC_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN to provision-secrets.yml to make this auto-satisfiable.
rules.description: Bot token for the single Telegram bot serving the whole fleet's CI notifications.
usedBy: telegram-pr-merged.yml (22 repos, calls the FuzeSDLC reusable with `secrets: inherit`)
rules.scenario: A PR merges on FuzePlan. telegram-pr-merged.yml calls izzywdev/FuzeSDLC/.github/workflows/reusable-telegram-pr-merged.yml with `secrets: inherit`, and the reusable posts the merge notification to the fleet chat.
rules.withoutIt: HARD FAIL, not a skip. The reusable declares `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: required: true` in its workflow_call secrets block, so a caller without it fails workflow-call validation.
rules.whyThisSharing: One bot, one token. Per-repo bots would fragment the notification channel for no benefit.
rules.note: NOT in FuzeSDLC's FLEET_SOURCED set, so provision-secrets.yml cannot supply it. Add SRC_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN to make the 11-repo gap auto-closable.

rules.name: TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
rules.notes: Destination chat, not a credential at all, but paired with the bot token everywhere it is used. Same FLEET_SOURCED gap.
rules.description: The destination chat id for fleet notifications. Not a credential at all -- an identifier -- but stored as a secret because it is passed alongside the bot token everywhere it is used.
rules.scenario: Paired with the bot token on every notification call.
rules.withoutIt: Same hard fail: the reusable declares it required: true.
rules.whyThisSharing: One destination chat.
rules.note: A prime candidate for an Actions VARIABLE rather than a secret -- it needs no rotation, and keeping it in the secret list dilutes the real rotation surface.

rules.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
rules.notes: Second rung of the model cascade (governance/model-cascade.md). Absence does not fail a run -- it removes a fallback. Fleet-declare it so the cascade is real everywhere rather than only on the six repos that happen to have it.
rules.description: A direct OpenAI API key. In the intended cascade it is the second rung behind the LiteLLM gateway.
usedBy: canonical templates only -- read by NO deployed FuzeInfra workflow
rules.scenario: Under the intended design, llm-endpoint probes the in-cluster gateway; if it is not ready the run falls back to a runner-local LiteLLM instance primed with this key, rather than failing.
rules.withoutIt: Nothing breaks today, because no deployed workflow reads it. If the cascade is adopted, its second rung would be missing.
rules.whyThisSharing: One OpenAI account key.
rules.note: Set in 6 repos and read by nothing. Either adopt the cascade or stop provisioning it -- a secret no code reads is rotation surface with no benefit.

rules.name: GEMINI_API_KEY
rules.notes: Third rung of the same cascade, referenced by claude.yml/a2a-maintain/mcp-maintain/governance-nightly templates. Present on FuzeSDLC alone today, so the cascade's bottom rung is fleet-wide fiction.
rules.description: A direct Google Gemini API key -- third rung of the intended model cascade.
usedBy: canonical templates only; read by no deployed workflow
rules.scenario: Same as OPENAI_API_KEY: the cascade's last resort if both the gateway and OpenAI are unavailable.
rules.withoutIt: Nothing breaks today. Under the intended cascade the bottom rung would be absent fleet-wide.
rules.whyThisSharing: One Google account key.
rules.note: Present in FuzeSDLC alone. governance/model-registry.md marks the Gemini rows UNVERIFIED, so its absence may be deliberate rather than an oversight -- confirm before provisioning.

rules.name: DESIGN_APPROVAL_DEPLOY_KEY
rules.notes: NOT propagatable, despite the fleet-wide gap. A GitHub deploy key is bound to ONE repository, so each of the 15 repos carrying design-approval.yml needs its own generated keypair registered as that repo's ruleset bypass actor. It exists in zero repos today, so the design-approval flip has never worked anywhere -- including in FuzeSDLC, which ships the workflow. Note FuzeFinance does the same job under the name RELEASE_BUMP_SSH_KEY: the standard has two names as well as no values.
rules.description: The private half of a PER-REPO SSH deploy key. Its public half is registered on ONE repo with write access, and that repo's branch ruleset carries a DeployKey bypass entry so the push is exempt from the pull_request and required_signatures rules. It carries no API scope.
rules.scenario: A designer clicks Approve inside a published HTML frame. That opens a prefilled issue labelled design-approval carrying feature, flow, decision and a `stamp` hash of the current frame files. design-approval.yml fires, confirms the clicker is a CODEOWNER, recomputes the stamp and checks it still matches, then must write build.flows[<flow>].approved=true into the frame manifest ON PROTECTED MAIN. A Contents-API commit with GITHUB_TOKEN would be rejected by the ruleset, so it pushes over SSH with this key, whose bypass entry exempts it. gate-frames-stamped.yml then treats that flow as approved for later PRs.
rules.withoutIt: The step fails fast with an explicit error rather than silently dropping the approval. The secret existed in ZERO repos until 2026-08-31, so the design-approval flip had never worked anywhere -- including in FuzeSDLC, which ships the workflow.
rules.whyThisSharing: Uniqueness falls out of what a deploy key IS. It is registered via POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/keys against exactly one repository and authenticates only that repo's SSH endpoint. Because this key WRITES to its own repo's protected branch -- unlike FUZESDLC_DEPLOY_KEY, which READS from one shared source -- no single value could mechanically work fleet-wide without registering the same public half everywhere, at which point one leak is a ruleset-bypass push credential on all of them at once.
rules.note: RULESET GOTCHA, verified 2026-08-31. GitHub has NO `DeployKeyId` bypass actor type and no per-key scoping. The only supported entry is `{actor_type: DeployKey, actor_id: null}` -- a BLANKET 'any write-access deploy key on this repo bypasses the ruleset' rule. So adding it grants bypass to every write deploy key on that repo, present and future. Today 13 of 14 affected repos hold exactly one write key (the design-approval one); FuzeSDLC holds two, so `fuzesdlc-deploy-key (provisioner)` also gained bypass. Adding any write deploy key to these repos is now a privilege grant. FuzeFinance has NO branch ruleset at all, so no bypass was needed -- and its default branch is unprotected.

rules.name: FUZEINFRA_DISPATCH_TOKEN
rules.notes: repository_dispatch into FuzeInfra's cluster-query.yml / infra-dispatch.yml -- the self-service read-only kubectl consuming repos use to verify their own deploys. Needed by any repo that deploys into the shared cluster.
rules.description: A token permitting repository_dispatch into izzywdev/FuzeInfra. The consumer-facing half of FuzeInfra's self-service cluster tooling.
usedBy: targets FuzeInfra's cluster-query.yml, infra-request-handler.yml and argocd-register.yml
rules.scenario: MendysRobotics has deployed and wants to verify its pods came up. Instead of asking a human to relay kubectl output, it fires a repository_dispatch at FuzeInfra, which runs a READ-ONLY kubectl on its behalf and returns the result. Mutating verbs, Secret reads and --raw are refused by tests/test_cluster_query_guard.py, because FuzeInfra's job logs are public.
rules.withoutIt: The consuming repo cannot verify its own deploys and falls back to asking a human.
rules.whyThisSharing: One token into one target repo. The privilege is bounded by what FuzeInfra's handler will DO, not by who holds the token -- which is why it is the right replacement for KUBE_CONFIG in the five ARC-only consumers.

rules.name: KUBE_CONFIG
rules.notes: SHARED TODAY, SHOULD NOT BE. One kubeconfig handed to six repos means six blast radii for one credential and no way to tell which repo used it. Correct end state is a per-repo, namespace-scoped ServiceAccount token (unique-value); until then treat every copy as prod-admin.
rules.description: A base64-encoded kubeconfig for the Contabo k3s PROD cluster. As minted today it is a full CLUSTER-ADMIN credential in every copy: runners/arc/ONBOARD-REPO.md prescribes `kubectl config view --raw | base64 -w0`, which dumps whatever context is active -- in every observed case the same admin credential humans and Argo CD use.
rules.scenario: FuzeSocial runs arc-register.yml to give itself a self-hosted runner. The job decodes KUBE_CONFIG on a GitHub-hosted runner and helm-installs a scale-set into arc-runners. That needs write on ONE namespace -- but the credential present is full admin, so the same job, or anyone who exfiltrates the secret via a compromised Action or a leaked log, could run `kubectl delete namespace fuzeinfra` or read every Secret in every namespace on shared prod.
rules.withoutIt: The consuming workflow cannot reach the cluster and fails or no-ops.
rules.whyThisSharing: Shared-value TODAY and wrong -- but the fix is not 20 unique kubeconfigs. Six of the eight referencing workflows need no cluster credential at all: five repos use it ONLY for ARC registration, which FuzeInfra can perform on their behalf via repository_dispatch (the cluster-query / infra-request-handler pattern, bounded by FUZEINFRA_DISPATCH_TOKEN); and FuzeFront's seal path needs only the sealed-secrets PUBLIC cert, since sealing is asymmetric encrypt-only. Target end state: KUBE_CONFIG exists in FuzeInfra only.
rules.note: HOLDERS (6): FuzeContact, FuzeHub, FuzeInfra, FuzeSales, FuzeService, FuzeSocial. FuzeFront and MendysRobotics REFERENCE it without holding it, so those two workflows have been inert, not working. Namespace-scoped ServiceAccount tokens are a target state, not current state -- every copy today is cluster-admin.

rules.name: FUZEFRONT_REGISTRATION_TOKEN
rules.notes: Bearer token from the fuzefront/fuzefront-registration Secret, consumed by @fuzefront/onboarding-kit. One issuer token, so shared by construction. Its in-cluster twin is already automated via governance/credential-handoff.json -- this is the CI-side copy.

rules.name: GHCR_PAT
rules.notes: ghcr.io push credential for repos that build images. Shared registry, shared credential -- but scope it to packages:write only.
rules.description: A GitHub PAT with packages scope for the shared ghcr.io registry.
usedBy: seal-secrets.yml in consuming repos -- sealed into an in-cluster imagePullSecret
rules.scenario: A repo's seal-secrets.yml seals this token into the Kubernetes imagePullSecret its Deployment references, so the cluster can pull private ghcr.io/izzywdev/* images.
rules.withoutIt: The pod cannot pull its image and stays in ImagePullBackOff.
rules.whyThisSharing: One shared registry, one pull identity. Scope it to packages:read where the consumer only pulls.
rules.note: CORRECTS AN EARLIER CLAIM that this looked unused. It IS used -- an earlier survey only looked at docker/login-action call sites, and its real job is sealing an imagePullSecret. Do not retire it.

rules.name: NPM_TOKEN
rules.notes: GitHub Packages publish for @fuzefront/* private packages. Every repo that ships a reusable npm package needs it; only FuzeFront has it today.

rules.name: NOTIFY_EMAIL_PASS
rules.notes: Gmail app password for CI notification mail. Same mailbox everywhere it appears.

rules.name: GH_TOKEN
rules.notes: Admin PAT. auto-merge.yml needs `gh pr merge --admin` to bypass the strict ruleset, which the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do. Being superseded by FUZE_AGENT_APP_*; do not propagate it further -- finish the App migration instead.

rules.name: JWT_SECRET
rules.notes: REVIEW. Shared only if FuzeInfra and FuzePicker genuinely validate tokens FuzeFront issues (one trust domain, one signing key). If they issue their OWN tokens, this must become unique-value per service -- a shared signing key lets any holder forge any other's tokens.
rules.description: TWO DIFFERENT credentials that share a name. In FuzeFront it is a genuine single-issuer HS256 signing key: FuzeFront's backend mints session tokens with it and FuzeFront's own middleware verifies them. In FuzePicker it is a separately generated, deliberately unshared secret used only to sign FuzePicker's own local username/password login tokens.
usedBy: FuzeFront backend/src/routes/auth.ts (sign) and its auth middleware (verify)
rules.scenario: A user signs into FuzeFront: its identity service signs an HS256 JWT and its own middleware verifies it -- correct single-trust-domain use. Separately, a FuzePicker user authenticated against FuzeFront is verified by FuzePicker CALLING FuzeFront's live /api/v1/security/session endpoint over HTTPS -- no local secret involved. FuzePicker's own JWT_SECRET only signs its unrelated local logins; requireSession.js actively relies on a FuzeFront token FAILING verification under FuzePicker's key.
rules.withoutIt: Token signing or verification fails in whichever service is missing its own value.
rules.whyThisSharing: SPLIT THE ENTRY. Within FuzeFront, sharing among FuzeFront's own services is correct and unavoidable under HS256 -- one issuer, one verifier, one key. ACROSS products it is not sharing at all: FuzePicker's value is independent by design and its code comments say so. Copying FuzeFront's signing key into FuzePicker would be pointless and a forgery risk if any future code path trusted it.
rules.note: CORRECTS AN EARLIER CLAIM that this was the cross-product M2M credential. Cross-product trust is already API-call-based, not secret-based. The real M2M path shipped in FuzeFront PR #837 (registerS2SClient, verifyMachineTokenViaJwks, Authentik client_credentials) and is FEATURE-FLAG GATED OFF behind `fuzefront.platform.s2s-jwks-auth`, with consumer migrations FuzeCall#29 and FuzeX#26 still open.

rules.name: PENPOT_MCP_URL
rules.notes: Design-tool MCP endpoint used by FuzeFront's design workflows only.
MCP endpoints/tokens consumed by provision.yml when provisioning managed agents. Only the two repos that actually run agent provisioning need them; FuzeSDLC is missing the whole set.

rules.name: MANAGED_AGENTS_API_KEY
rules.notes: Console key with the managed-agents beta, used by provision.yml. Absent -> the reusable provisioning workflow skips rather than fails.
rules.description: A direct Anthropic Console key carrying the managed-agents beta entitlement. Distinct from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and NOT interchangeable with a gateway key.
rules.scenario: A merge touches agent-templates/roles/**. provision-sync.yml calls provision.yml, which reconciles the deployed managed agents against their definitions using Anthropic's Managed Agents control-plane API. The workflows map this key into ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at the step level.
rules.withoutIt: The reusable provisioning workflow SKIPS (no fail). Agent definitions drift from their deployed counterparts silently.
rules.whyThisSharing: One Console account with the entitlement.
rules.note: A legitimately required DIRECT key, not a redundant copy and not a gateway fallback: LiteLLM does not proxy the Managed Agents control-plane API. Do not 'consolidate' it into LITELLM_FUZE_KEY.

rules.name: FUZE_SECRETS_PROVISIONER_APP_ID
rules.notes: The fleet secret-provisioner App. Holds secrets:write on EVERY repo -- the single highest-privilege credential in the fleet. It must exist on FuzeSDLC and nowhere else; a copy elsewhere is a fleet-wide compromise path.
rules.description: App ID of the `izzywdev-fleet-secrets-provisioner` GitHub App (App ID 4737094, install 156968330), which holds secrets:write + metadata:read on every repo it can reach.
rules.scenario: provision-secrets.yml mints a fleet-wide installation token from this App and runs scripts/provision_secrets.py, which seals each source value to each repo's public key and PUTs the ciphertext.
rules.withoutIt: Fleet secret provisioning cannot run; every secret goes back to being set by hand.
rules.whyThisSharing: Single holder. The highest-privilege credential in the fleet -- a copy anywhere else is a fleet-wide compromise path.
rules.note: Replaced the fine-grained PAT FUZE_SECRETS_PROVISIONER_TOKEN (#677). KNOWN DEFECT as of 2026-08-31: the App token has no user, so provision_secrets.py's `/user/repos` discovery call fails silently under allow_fail=True and only the PUBLIC repo listing survives -- run 33399253601 reached 5 of 22 repos. Fixed by FuzeSDLC PR #252 (adds /installation/repositories). Until that merges, treat any provisioning run as covering public repos only.

rules.notes: Permit.io authorization control plane.

rules.name: INTERNAL_PROVISION_SECRET
rules.notes: Shared secret for FuzeFront's internal provisioning endpoint.

rules.name: RELEASE_BUMP_SSH_KEY
rules.notes: Write key used by FuzeFront's release version-bump commit.
rules.description: A write SSH deploy key on FuzeFront serving FOUR unrelated jobs under one credential: release bump, fuzequality release, sealed-secret commit, and (until FuzeFront PR #871) design approval.
rules.scenario: FuzeFront's release job pushes a version-bump commit to protected main using this key's ruleset bypass.
rules.withoutIt: Those FuzeFront jobs cannot push to the protected branch.
rules.whyThisSharing: Single repo, so not shared across the fleet -- but overloaded WITHIN the repo, which is its own problem: no trust separation (design approval is triggered by a web-page click, the lowest-trust input, and shared a credential with the release pipeline), rotation coupling (rotating for one breaks three, so it never gets rotated), and no attribution (four flows, one key).
rules.note: CORRECTS governance/secrets-policy.json's earlier claim that FuzeFinance renames the design-approval key to this. FALSE -- FuzeFinance uses the standard DESIGN_APPROVAL_DEPLOY_KEY name; FuzeFront is the repo that overloads RELEASE_BUMP_SSH_KEY. FuzeFront PR #871 removes the design-approval consumer. The remaining three should move to fuze-agent App installation tokens via the Contents API (server-side signed, satisfying required_signatures with no bypass actor), after which this key can be deleted and revoked.

Android/Play signing keystores for the packaged mobile shells. Per-app by definition and must never leave the repo that publishes that app.
Deploy-shape configuration stored as secrets. Most of these are not secret at all -- candidates for Actions VARIABLES, which are readable and auditable.
Contabo API credentials driving the cluster autoscaler. Node lifecycle + billing -- FuzeInfra only.
Terraform remote-state backend + variables. FuzeInfra is the only repo that runs Terraform.
k3s server URL + node join token. A node token is cluster-join capability -- treat as prod-critical.
Airflow admin password + Fernet key for the shared workflow engine.
Cloudflare account-level credentials + the tunnel that is the ONLY ingress path to prod. Global API key especially: account-wide, unscopable, FuzeInfra only.
Zone-scoped. MendysRobotics manages a different zone than FuzeInfra, so each holder should carry a token scoped to ITS zone -- not a copy of the other's.
Superuser/admin passwords for the shared datastores and admin UIs. Applications get their OWN per-service role (unique-value) -- they must never receive these.
Google/Gmail credentials backing Cloudflare Access OTP and notification mail.
Platform-operation credentials. LITELLM_MASTER_KEY in particular mints every downstream LiteLLM key and was the subject of the 2026-07-29 public-log leak -- it must exist in exactly one place.

VERIFY. If FuzeInfra and FuzeFront hold the same IAM user's keys, split them into per-repo IAM principals -- or better, replace both with OIDC role assumption (FuzeHub already uses AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, which is the right shape).

FuzeKeys' own datastore credentials. Also the fleet's worst case of secret-sprawl: 12 secrets encoding one Postgres and one Redis connection. Collapse to a single DATABASE_URL + REDIS_URL and move the host/port/name/prefix parts to Actions variables.
MendysRobotics service credentials (Postgres + Mongo roles, product API key).
Chrome Web Store publishing credentials, bound to one extension listing.
Per-service datastore role. Exactly the right pattern: the app gets its own role, not the shared superuser.
Application signing/encryption material. Sharing these across services would let each decrypt the others' data.
Repo-scoped tokens/keys. Unique by construction -- each is issued against one repo or one Argo destination.
Host access for a repo's own deployment target (MendysRoboticsWP's WordPress host, FuzeFront's build host).
Third-party product credentials owned by the consuming repo. Could technically be shared; keeping them per-repo keeps revocation cheap.

$fields.description: What the credential IS and what it grants.
$fields.usedBy: Workflows or code that consume it.
$fields.scenario: One concrete walkthrough of it doing its job.
$fields.withoutIt: The observed failure mode when absent -- hard fail, silent skip, or degrade.
$fields.whyThisSharing: Why the sharing verdict follows from what the credential is.
$fields.note: Corrections, migration state, and things otherwise relearned the hard way.
$fields.$comment: GitHub Actions secrets have NO native description field -- the REST API stores only name/created_at/updated_at, and the same is true of Dependabot secrets and Actions variables. These fields ARE that description, and scripts/secrets_inventory.py renders them into the reference section of its report.
